question: Is the haze in Johor Bahru worse than Singapore right now?
name: Claude
answer:
Let me get the latest Johor figures from the Oct 16–17 sources.**Short answer: no. Right now they're about the same, and Singapore may be slightly worse.** Both are in the "unhealthy" range.

**Singapore (NEA, 17 Oct, morning)**
- Singapore's 24-hour PSI was 140 to 185 across its five regions as of 10:00 am on 17 Oct 2026. Central was highest, in the Unhealthy band. That figure comes from an unofficial aggregator site.
- At 7:00 am the 24-hour PSI was unhealthy across Singapore, with a high of 191 in Central.

**Johor (Malaysia DOE API, 17 Oct, 9:30 am)**
- Pasir Gudang had the highest reading in the country at 196.
- Other Johor areas were Larkin (177), Pengerang (174), Kota Tinggi (172), Batu Pahat (170), Tangkak (168), Segamat (161) and Kluang (159).
- Johor Bahru itself (Larkin) is around 177.

**Comparison**
- Singapore's highest regional reading is about 185–191. Johor's highest is 196, in Pasir Gudang, and Johor Bahru proper is about 177.
- All of these are in the 101–200 "unhealthy" band. The two places are within roughly 10–20 points of each other.
- Singapore's PSI and Malaysia's API are separate indices. They are similar, but they aren't strictly the same scale.
- Both are 24-hour averages, so they lag behind what you'd feel outdoors at the moment.
- Johor was worse a day or two earlier. Pasir Gudang hit a "very unhealthy" 205 on the morning of 16 Oct. It has since eased slightly.
- One live-tracker snapshot from 15 Oct showed Singapore at a US AQI of 283 and Johor Bahru at 261. That is a different scale, but it also had Singapore slightly higher.

**If you're crossing the Causeway:** expect similar conditions on both sides. Reduce strenuous outdoor activity, and consider an N95 mask if you're elderly, pregnant, have heart or lung conditions, or are travelling with children.

Readings update hourly, so check NEA (haze.gov.sg) and Malaysia's APIMS portal for the live numbers.

# Haze worsens nationwide, Johor leads with most number of areas recording unhealthy API
PETALING JAYA: Haze conditions worsened nationwide as of 11am on Tuesday (Oct 6), with 23 areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, up from 21 as of 8am, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).

Johor was the worst hit, with all eight of its areas in the unhealthy range and Batu Pahat recording the highest reading nationwide at 193.

The others were Segamat (170), Kluang (170), Larkin (166), Pasir Gudang (166), Tangkak (166), Kota Tinggi (157) and Pengerang (156), with seven of the eight Johor areas recording higher readings than at 8am.



Outside Johor, the highest readings were recorded in Nilai (164) and Seremban (161) in Negeri Sembilan, followed by Bandaraya Melaka (158), Putrajaya (155) and Balok Baru Kuantan in Pahang (155).

API readings of between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 m

# Haze: Pasir Gudang hits very unhealthy API reading, 33 unhealthy nationwide
PETALING JAYA: Pasir Gudang in Johor recorded a very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 205 as of 8am on Friday (Oct 16), the highest nationwide and up from 186 as of 7pm on Thursday (Oct 17), according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).

It is the only area in the very unhealthy range, while Klang in Selangor, which recorded the highest reading of 194 on Thursday, is now at 181.

In total, 33 areas recorded unhealthy or worse readings, the same as at 7pm on Thursday.

Of the 31 areas that remained unhealthy or worse, 19 recorded lower readings than on Thursday evening, while 10 recorded higher readings and two were unchanged.



Johor had the most affected areas with eight, followed by Selangor with six, Perak with five and Negri Sembilan, Melaka and Pahang with three each.

The Johor areas were Pasir Gudang (205), Larkin (193), Pengerang (175), Batu Pahat (173), Kluang (170), Tangkak (165), Kota Tinggi (163) and Segamat (159), with five of the eight recording higher readings than on Thursday evening.
